fixes.what: The 24 August 1335 Treaty of Trentschin is recorded as a confidence-3 gain of the whole of Silesia from the Kingdom of Poland, but no land changed hands.
fixes.why: Treaty of Trentschin page: Casimir's representatives 'renounced all claims to Silesia in favour of Bohemia'; the Silesian duchies were already John's vassals (1327, 1329; /ledger/14, /ledger/16) and stay vassal tint until 1348 in this dossier's own keyframes 15-16, and the same page dates Jawor (Świdnica-Jawor) to Bohemia only in 1392 (/ledger/32). As written the event draws all Silesia as direct Bohemian land from 1335, including Świdnica-Jawor, and demands a phantom 1335 loss of Silesia in the kingdom-of-poland dossier.
fixes.fix: Remove the gain (keep the treaty and its quotes in the war 'Bohemian-Polish dispute over Silesia' and in certainty notes), or, if a page dates it, replace it with a gain of the Duchy of Wrocław only, on Henry VI's death in 1335 (counterpart the Wrocław duchy, not Poland).

fixes.what: The Egerland is gained twice (1266 and 1322) with no loss in between.
fixes.why: /ledger/6 quotes the Kingdom page: 'All of Ottokar's German possessions were lost in 1276'; the Egerland page has Cheb 'a free imperial city since 1277'; the Kingdom and Lands pages say it was 'obtained by King Wenceslaus II between 1291 and 1305' and 'definitely given in pawn to Bohemia by King Louis IV in 1322'.
fixes.fix: Add the Egerland to the 1276 loss (or a separate 1276/1277 loss, counterpart holy-roman-empire-minor-states), then either a confidence-1 regain under Wenceslaus II (1291-1305) or keep only the 1322 gain; the 1279-1321 keyframes then need a correction for the Egerland.
